mappings.why: Names neither a source nor a series: not a venue, not an instrument, not a statistic. The single largest group on the 18 September catalogue at 18 instances, so this is the common case and not an edge one. A 300-second window on a '1-minute candle' does not resolve it either -- the two disagree about the period. Nothing here can be mapped without inventing the deployer's intent.

A bare identifier, retained as written. Whatever 'xyz:CL' denotes to its deployer, it is not a price series this project can name, and guessing at a crude-oil ticker would be exactly the silent resolution PLAN section 6 forbids.

Names Pyth plainly, and the template metadata says 'This market must refer to the price of a Hyperliquid perp.' The description and the restriction contradict each other, and the deployer-actions page makes a contradiction slashable by validators -- so which one governs is not this project's to decide. 15 instances. Mapping it to pyth:BTC/USD:price-twap:90s would be a reading the venue's own template denies; mapping it to hl:perp:BTC:mark-twap:90s would be a reading the description denies.
The same contradiction as the BTC/USD row, on 9 instances. Listed separately because a mapping is keyed by the exact description and nothing here is inferred from a family resemblance.

The same contradiction, on 9 instances, and additionally an index rather than a crypto pair: there is no Hyperliquid perp for US100 at all, so the template restriction cannot be satisfied even in principle.
As the US100 row: 9 instances, an index with no corresponding Hyperliquid perp.

Names the venue (Hyperliquid), the instrument (BTC perp) and the statistic (trade price) explicitly, and the 90-second window matches the template's own TWAP field. The trade series, not the mark: the description says 'trade'. Interpreted and not confirmed -- no deployer has confirmed it in writing -- so it surfaces in every result that rests on it.

Names the instrument as Hyperliquid spells it in its own catalogue (BTC-USDC) and the statistic as the mark. 8 instances. A one-second TWAP is a single observation in practice, and it is recorded as declared rather than collapsed to the instantaneous mark, because the template says seconds:1 and a mapping states what the venue said.

As the row above, with 'perp' said explicitly and a 60-second window. Kept as its own mapping rather than folded into 'BTC-USDC mark': the descriptions differ, and a mapping is keyed by what the venue wrote.
The HYPE perp mark on a 3-second window.

THE SAME TEXT AS THE ROW ABOVE WITH A TRAILING SPACE, and a different window. Both are live on the 18 September catalogue from one venue under one template. Kept as two mappings deliberately: a lookup that trimmed whitespace would merge two descriptions the venue sent separately, and would then answer for a string nobody wrote. If these are meant to be one market, that is the deployer's to say.
